Between 8.17 p.m. and 8.32 p.m., four Tiki-Taka zones will come alive with Messi, Suarez, De Paul, the Chief Minister and Rahul Gandhi actively engaging with children, passing the ball, offering encouragement and sharing moments. The clinic will culminate in a special penalty shootout with Messi, with organiser Anuttam Reddy donning the goalkeeper’s gloves.
A parade walk around the stadium will be followed, as Messi, Revanth Reddy, Rahul Gandhi, Suarez and De Paul acknowledging the fans. The dignitaries will then assemble on a stage erected on the ground, where guests would be introduced as per protocol.
During the felicitation ceremony, the GOAT Cup will be presented by Lionel Messi to the winning team, while Rahul Gandhi will hand over the cup to the other participating team. The Chief Minister will felicitate Messi with a gift and shawl, while Parvathi Reddy and others will honour Luis Suarez and Rodrigo De Paul.
This will be followed by remarks by the Chief Minister and Rahul Gandhi, and the programme will conclude at 9 pm with all dignitaries exiting the stadium by 9 p.m.

title: Income Tax department sends SMS/emails for bogus political donation claims
summary: The Income Tax department warns taxpayers about bogus political donation claims via SMS and email advisories to correct deductions.
content:
The Income Tax department has started sending SMS and email advisories to taxpayers for wrongful deduction claims related to unrecognised political parties or charitable institutions, the Finance Ministry said on Saturday (December 13, 2025).
The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) said through data analysis it has observed that huge amount of bogus claims have been made on account of donations to Registered Unrecognised Political Parties (RUPPs) or Charitable Institutions and reduced their tax obligations and have also claimed bogus refunds.
"A targeted NUDGE campaign has been launched as a taxpayer-friendly measure, providing them opportunity to update their ITRs and withdraw wrong claims, if any. SMSs and Email advisories are being issued from 12th December 2025 to such taxpayers on their registered mobile numbers and emails," the Finance Ministry said in a statement.
The CBDT said that evidence gathered from enforcement actions indicated that RUPPs, many of which were non-filers, non-operational at their registered addresses, and are not engaged in any political activity, were being used as conduits for routing funds, hawala transactions, cross-border remittances, and issuing bogus receipts for donations. The CBDT carried out follow-up searches against some of these RUPPs and trusts and gathered incriminating evidence in respect of bogus donations by individuals and bogus CSR by companies, it said.
CBDT's data analytics indicated that many taxpayers are suspected to be indulged in claiming deductions for donation made to suspicious entities or have not provided relevant information to ascertain the genuineness of the entities.
A large number of taxpayers have already revised their Income Tax Returns for the current AY that is 2025-26, and have filed updated ITRs for past years, it added.
"Every taxpayer is advised to ensure that correct mobile and email IDs are mentioned in their filings with the Department so that they do not miss out any communication," the CBDT said.

title: 10 Manipur BJP MLAs fly to Delhi to meet party's central leaders
summary: Ten Manipur BJP MLAs, including ex-CM N Biren Singh, meet central leaders in Delhi amid hopes for a positive government formation.
content:
Ten Manipur BJP MLAs, including ex-CM N Biren Singh and speaker Th Satyabrata Singh, on Saturday (December 13, 2025) left for Delhi to attend a meeting with the party's central leadership.
The former CM said he was hopeful that "some positive decision" would be taken at the meeting.
"I am expecting positive things for a better Manipur. I hope a positive decision will be taken at the meeting. As far as the formation of the government is concerned, it will be known only after the meeting," he said.
MLA Kh Joykishan Singh said the meeting is expected to be related to the government formation.
MLA RK Imo Singh said, "We have been called for a meeting tomorrow. Let's see what will happen. We don't have much detail."
Some other BJP MLAs are also in the national capital for "personal reasons", a party leader said.
BJP has 37 MLAs in the 60-member Manipur assembly.
The State has been under the President's Rule since February, after Biren Singh resigned amid criticisms over his government's handling of the ethnic violence that broke out in May 2023.

title: Second airport for Bengaluru: Tenders invited for feasibility study, says Minister M.B. Patil
summary: Bengaluru's second airport feasibility study tender invites consultancy firms to assess potential sites and develop a comprehensive report.
content:
The Karnataka State Industrial and Infrastructure Development Corporation (KSIIDC) has invited tenders to select an expert consultancy firm to prepare a location suitability and comprehensive technical and financial feasibility report for the proposed second international airport for the State capital.
The last date for submission of applications is January 12, 2026, Infrastructure Development Minister M.B. Patil said on Saturday (December 13, 2025) in a release.
Giving details, he said the State government has identified sites at Choodahalli and Somanahalli on Kanakapura Road, along with another location near Nelamangala, for the proposed airport.
A high-level team from the Airports Authority of India has inspected these locations and submitted a preliminary report. The consultancy firm selected through the tender process will be required to submit a detailed technical and financial feasibility report to the government within five months, he added.
Firms that have executed projects worth at least ₹250 crore annually over the past five years, and have handled or prepared consultancy reports for a minimum of five projects in the relevant sector, will be eligible to participate in the tender, Mr. Patil said.
The selected consultancy firm will study parameters such as rainfall patterns, topography, availability of power, water supply, sewerage and waste management infrastructure, surrounding population, regional development, and noise pollution likely to arise from airport operations at all three identified locations.
The Minister noted that the feasibility report must also include details of the estimated cost of developing the proposed airport, the extent of land required, and approvals to be obtained from various authorities, including the Ministry of Defence and the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA). The report will also assess the impact of a new airport on industries, tourism and public mobility in the region.
The consultancy firm will further examine existing connectivity to the proposed sites and the infrastructure that would need to be developed after the airport is constructed. In addition, cargo handling and passenger services, along with their economic viability, will be studied. Based on a comprehensive assessment of all three locations, the firm will submit its recommendation on the most suitable site for the second airport, he explained in the release.
Mr. Patil said Kempegowda International Airport currently ranks second in the country in terms of passenger density. By 2033, the State will require another airport, and efforts have therefore been initiated well in advance with a forward-looking approach.
At present, New Delhi and Mumbai ahave two airports each. Once the feasibility report is received, the government will decide on the next course of action, the Minister stated.

title: Delhi HC rejects scientist’s plea for mandatory work from home under GRAP
summary: Delhi HC dismisses scientist's plea for work from home due to air pollution, stating no enforceable service rights exist.
content:
The Delhi High Court has dismissed a petition filed by a Scientist-E employed with an autonomous telecommunications technology development centre under the Department of Telecommunications, who had sought permission to work from home citing health issues arising from severe air pollution in the national capital.
The petitioner, Shubham Verma, approached the court claiming that despite the Commission for Air Quality Management prescribing work from home for at least 50% of employees in offices across Delhi from November 21, 2025, his office failed to comply with the instructions.
According to the plea, Mr. Verma developed medical issues on November 23, 2025, due to the prevailing air quality conditions and was advised by a doctor to “avoid dust and smoke exposure”. He claimed that despite seeking permission to work from home between November 23 and November 27, 2025, no response was received from his employer.
The petitioner sought directions to allow him to work from home until the organisation could certify that indoor air quality was within permissible limits, and further requested that the period be treated as on duty even if he was unable to physically report to office.
Justice Sachin Datta, in an order passed on December 9, said he was not persuaded by the arguments advanced on behalf of Mr. Verma. The court observed that the Graded Response Action Plan (GARP) and its attendant guidelines are regulatory measures intended to curb polluting activities and empower authorities such as the Commission for Air Quality Management and the Delhi Pollution Control Committee to issue directions.
“No doubt, the said regulatory measures are required to be implemented scrupulously. However, the same cannot be construed as conferring rights on central government officials or employees against their employers in derogation of their service conditions,” Justice Datta observed.
The court further noted that the relevant GRAP guideline dated November 21, 2025, vests discretion with the central government regarding the grant of work from home and does not impose a mandatory obligation.
Terming the petitioner’s claim of an automatic entitlement to work from home as “misplaced”, the court nonetheless observed that in view of his medical exigencies, he would be at liberty to request his employer for a transfer out of Delhi.

title: Will make Bastar the most developed tribal region by 2030, says Shah
summary: Amit Shah announces plans to develop Bastar into India's most advanced tribal region by 2030, promoting peace and progress.
content:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Saturday (December 13, 2025) said that India stood on the verge of eliminating Maoism by March 2026 and that the government has now set its sights on making Chhattisgarh’s Bastar the most developed tribal division in the country by 2030.
“Our resolve is to free the entire land of India, and especially the Bastar region, from Maoism. But we won’t stop there. I declare before all of you today that Kanker, Kondagaon, Bastar, Sukma, Bijapur, Dantewada, and Narayanpur — these seven districts of the Bastar division—will become the most developed tribal districts in the country by December 2030,” he said during his speech at the concluding ceremony of Bastar Olympics.
Bastar Olympics is an annual mega sports event in Jagdalpur in which participants from all seven districts of the region compete in various sports events. This year it also saw participation from surrendered Maoists.
Asserting that peace only can pave the road for development, he laid out the contours of the 2030 vision which he said would include basic amenities, expanding services and specialised schemes.
“..every household will have access to basic amenities, every village will be connected by roads, every village will have electricity, banking facilities will be available within a 5-km radius, and most importantly, both the central and state governments of the Bharatiya Janata Party will work to establish a network of Primary Health Centers (PHCs) and Community Health Centers (CHCs),” he said.
Mr. Shah also said that units for processing forest produce will be set up here on a cooperative basis, and the government would also target increasing incomes through dairy production.
“We will also establish new industries, higher education institutions, top-notch sports schools, and as many hospitals as needed in Bastar. Special schemes will be launched to combat malnutrition. And we will also bring in excellent rehabilitation schemes for those who have surrendered, laid down their arms and returned from Maoism, and for all those who have been injured due to Maoism,” he added.
Mr. Shah lauded all participants, especially mentioning the surrendered Maoists, who competed in the Bastar Olympics, even as he reiterated his appeal to all Maoists to lay down arms.
“When I received the news that more than 700 surrendered Maoists, our brothers and sisters, had participated in these games, I was overjoyed. 700 young people whose lives could have been ruined by falling into the trap of Maoism have now found a new path through sports,” he said.

title: Two labourers mowed down by car on NICE Road
summary: Two labourers killed in a hit-and-run on NICE Road, Bengaluru; driver arrested following police investigation.
content:
Two daily wage labourers were killed in a hit-and-run incident on NICE Road in west Bengaluru on Friday (December 12, 2025) evening. The deceased have been identified as Rangamma (45) and Chowdamma (50), contracted labourers hailing from the Yadgir district.
On Saturday morning, the Kengeri Traffic Police arrested a man identified as Satyanarayana, a resident of Khatriguppe. The car allegedly involved in the incident has been seized.
The incident occurred around 6.15 p.m. on Friday (December 12), when the women were crossing the road some distance away from the toll plaza near Hosakerehalli. Satyanarayana, who was reportedly driving at high speed towards Magadi Road, allegedly mowed down both women and sped away without stopping.
A police officer investigating the case said the women had finished work and were heading home when the incident took place. “There was another person with the deceased who cautioned them against crossing the road at that spot, as it was unsafe, but they went ahead,” the officer toldThe Hindu. “We took up a hit-and-run case and traced the car by Friday night. The accused was taken into custody on Saturday morning,” he added.

title: Modi government 'master' at renaming schemes: Congress hits out at Centre over MGNREGA name change
summary: Congress criticizes Modi government for renaming MGNREGA, questioning the need to remove Mahatma Gandhi's name from the scheme.
content:
With the Cabinet approving a Bill to rename the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), the Congress on Saturday (December 13, 2025) said the PM Modi government is a "master" at renaming schemes and asked "what is wrong with the name Mahatma Gandhi" that it had to take this step.
Reacting to the development, Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh said the Modi government is a "master" at renaming schemes and laws.
"They renamed the Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan to Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, and the rural LPG distribution programme to Ujjwala. They are experts in re-packaging and branding," he toldPTI.
"They hate Pandit Nehru but it seems they also hate Mahatma Gandhi. What's wrong with the name Mahatma Gandhi, why rename the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act to Pujya Bapu Employment Guarantee Scheme?" Mr. Ramesh said.
The Union Cabinet on Friday (December 12) approved a Bill to rename the MGNREGA and increase the number of work days, sources said. According to them, the scheme will now be renamed as 'Poojya Bapu Grameen Rozgar Yojna', and the number of work days under it would be increased from 100 days at present to 125 days.
Congress general secretary in-charge organisation K.C. Venugopal said the PM, who once called MGNREGA a "monument of failure", is now renaming it to claim credit for the revolutionary scheme.
"It's yet another way of erasing Mahatma Gandhi from our national psyche, especially from the villages, where, he said, India's soul resides," he alleged.
"This move is also nothing but a cosmetic change to paper over the deliberate neglect being meted out to this scheme," Mr. Venugopal said onX.
MGNREGA workers have been demanding higher wages, but the Centre has been reducing allocated funds for the scheme year after year, he said.
"The arrears keep piling up, and it seems to be a carefully planned strategy to engineer a slow death for the scheme. In reality, this government has no intent of delivering welfare - and is merely putting up a pretence when it has run out of ideas," Mr. Venugopal alleged.
"But Mr Modi, rename it all you want, the people know it was Dr Manmohan Singh ji and Smt Sonia Gandhi ji who brought this transformative scheme to every village of India," he said.
The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme, better known as MGNREGA or NREGA, is a flagship scheme of the government aimed at enhancing livelihood security of households in the rural areas by providing at least 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in a financial year to every household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work. It was enacted in 2005.

title: IFFK 2025: ‘Palestine 36’ portrays the historical context of current conflicts
summary: Palestine 36 is the opening film of the 30th International Film Festival of Kerala
content:
Palestine 36, as the name signifies, is set in 1936, but almost every other sequence makes our minds travel to the present. It is not just because the contemporary conflicts in that land are rooted in the past century, but also due to the stark similarity of the indignities heaped upon the Palestinian people back then to the present.Palestine 36, the opening film of the 30th International Film Festival of Kerala, is being screened as part of a package of Palestinian films touching upon the ongoing conflicts.
The film is directed by Annemarie Jacir, whoseWajibwon the Suvarna Chakoram at the IFFK in 2017. While Wajib told the story of the fragile relationship between an estranged father and son to subtly paint a compelling portrait of contemporary Palestinian society,Palestine 36is set around the building up of a rebellion of the indigenous Palestinian people in 1936 against British imperialism and the Zionist takeover of large tracts of land that have belonged to Palestinians. Interspersed with grainy, archival-like footage of Israeli settlers arriving at Palestine are the sequences of happenings at the micro-level.
In one telling passage, the filmmaker focuses extensively on a raid of British forces on a village, whose inhabitants have been questioning the expansion of settlers into their farmlands, a raid marked by acts of cruelty. The film does not paint all Palestinians as concerned about resisting the imperialists. Among them are those who are passive and minding their own business, as well as the elites who are not averse to collaborating with the Zionists.
The British have among them too few whose conscience is pricked by the scale of the injustice that their side has inflicted upon the natives, although one doubts whether the kind of dramatic confrontations at the high table that the film portrays would have actually taken place in real life. Parts of the film does convey the impression of the screenwriter trying to use the film to educate the various historical layers of the conflict, but the strong emotional undercurrents work in the film’s favour.
Abdullah M. Abu Shawesh, the Palestinian Ambassador to India, said at the opening ceremony of the festival that it was the British empire which planted the seeds of the Palestinian misery, through the Balfour Declaration of 1917.Palestine 36depicts the initial sprouting of those seeds and the slow erosion of the rights of the people belonging to that land.

title: Vignan University holds Bala Mahotsav in Narasaraopet
summary: Vignan University hosts Bala Mahotsav in Narasaraopet, promoting creativity and teamwork among 2,000 participating students from 56 schools.
content:
Narasaraopet MP and vice-chairperson of Vignan institutions Lavu Sri Krishna Devarayalu called on students to cultivate diverse thinking from childhood, stressing creativity and innovation to succeed in a competitive world.
Addressing the valedictory event of the two-day Vignan Bala Mahotsav zonal competitions at Kodela Sivaprasad Stadium in Narasaraopet on Saturday (December 13), he urged students to balance academics with one indoor game, one outdoor sport and a personal hobby, while upholding self-respect and integrity.
MLA Chadalavada Aravind Babu said such festivals build teamwork, resilience and leadership. Over 2,000 students from 56 schools competed, with winners receiving trophies, certificates and cash prizes during vibrant cultural celebrations.

title: Sister-in-law of K.K. Ragesh defeated in CPI(M) stronghold
summary: CPI(M) candidate A. Anisha, sister-in-law of K.K. Ragesh, suffers defeat in Munderi panchayat elections amid internal dissent.
content:
In a major setback to the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] in its stronghold, Munderi panchayat president and party candidate A. Anisha was defeated in the local body elections.
Contesting from Ward 9 of Parothumchal, Anisha lost to UDF candidate P. Ashraf by a margin of 105 votes.
Munderi is considered the political bastion of CPI(M) district secretary K.K. Ragesh. Anisha, his sister-in-law, was fielded as the party candidate amid strong opposition within the CPI(M), with allegations of nepotism triggering dissent.
The discontent culminated in the emergence of a CPI(M) rebel candidate in Munderi panchayat, a factor that is believed to have contributed to the party’s defeat in the ward.

title: ₹479-crore project to develop ‘priority road corridors' in Vizag and Vijayawada
summary: ₹479-crore project to develop 110-km of priority road corridors in Vizag and Vijayawada under City Roads Improvement Program.
content:
The Municipal Administration & Urban Development (MA&UD) Department on Saturday accorded administrative sanction for implementing two pilot projects in Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada, costing about ₹479 crore, under the first phase of the City Roads Improvement Program (CRIP).
MA&UD Principal Secretary S. Suresh Kumar said in a press release that the two cities would have 110-km of priority urban corridors — 88.54 km in Visakhapatnam costing ₹306.95 crore and 23.54 km in Vijayawada estimated to cost ₹171.14 crore, for which the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) and Vijayawada Municipal Corporation (VMC) would notify their Requests for Proposals (RFPs) next week.
The CRIP is aimed at overhauling the condition of city roads across the State, with priority to quality, structural integrity, safety, and contractor accountability for a 10-year period, and it follows the Design-Build-Finance-Operate-Transfer (DBFOT) – Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM), which is widely regarded as one of the most efficient PPP structures for ensuring quality, transparency, and sustained asset maintenance.
Under HAM, 40% of the project cost will be released during the 12-month construction period against verified milestones and the balance 60% over a 10-year Operations & Maintenance (O&M) period through semi-annual annuities. This model incentivises the concessionaires to prioritise durable construction to reduce long-term maintenance liabilities.
The CRIP includes comprehensive and integrated redevelopment of streets, moving beyond road surface improvement to a full-scale transformation of the urban corridor ecosystem comprising capital and O&M works.
“The AP Urban Infrastructure Asset Management Limited has been appointed Independent Engineer for the CRIP,” Mr. Suresh Kumar said, adding that the RFP structure had been made contractor-friendly to encourage participation by both standalone and consortium-based bidders, including capable local firms.

title: Arunachal accident: 11 more bodies retrieved from site
summary: Eleven more bodies recovered from Arunachal Pradesh accident site, bringing total to 17; search for one missing person continues.
content:
Eleven more bodies were retrieved on Saturday (December 13, 2025) fromthe deep gorge in Arunachal Pradesh's Anjaw district, where a mini-truck on which 22 labourers from Assam were travelling fell, an official said.
With this, 17 bodies have been recovered from the accident site, Anjaw's deputy commissioner Milo Kojin said.
He said three more bodies will be brought out on Sunday (December 14, 2025).
The operation, being conducted by a joint team of the NDRF and Army, resumed at 6 a.m.
"The retrieval process was extremely difficult because of the treacherous terrain, and the gorge is very deep," Mr. Kojin said.
The operation was suspended around 4 p.m. due to low visibility and will be resumed on Sunday (December 14) morning, he said.
"One person is still missing, and a search operation will be carried out tomorrow," he added.
The accident happened on the evening of December 8, around 40 km from Hayuliang towards Chaglagam in the district. On the evening of December 10, one survivor managed to climb out of the gorge and reach a nearby Border Roads Task Force (BRTF) labour camp, following which the authorities were alerted.
Six bodies were recovered from the gorge on Friday (December 12) and handed over to their families on Saturday.

title: Minor girl introduced to drugs by Instagram ‘friends’ in Guntur
summary: A 17-year-old girl in Guntur was introduced to drugs by Instagram friends, leading to her mother's suicide attempt and police intervention.
content:
A 17-year-old Intermediate student from Chinna Bazar area in Guntur city was allegedly introduced to drugs by two youth she met on Instagram, according to the Lalapet police.
On learning about her addiction, her mother tried to end her life and was rushed to the Guntur Government General Hospital, where she is undergoing treatment. IGP (EAGLE) Ake Ravi Krishna and Guntur Superintendent of Police Vakul Jindal visited the woman at the hospital and enquired about her health.
Mr. Ravi Krishna said strict action will be taken against the culprits. Mr. Vakul Jindal said a special team has been formed to probe the case and identify those who supplied drugs to the minor. He noted that about 150 drug users were identified and booked over the past three months and that efforts were under way to trace the suppliers and peddlers.
Police said the minor will be provided counselling and treatment at a de-addiction centre.

title: CPI(M) rebel candidate wins Kara ward in Payyanur municipality
summary: CPI(M) rebel C. Vaishak wins Payyanur's Kara ward election, defeating LDF candidate by 458 votes amid party dissent.
content:
In a keenly watched contest, a CPI(M) rebel candidate emerged victorious in Ward 36 (Kara ward) of the Payyanur municipal election. Former CPI(M) branch secretary and DYFI leader C. Vaishak defeated the LDF candidate by a margin of 458 votes.
Vaishak secured the win with the backing of a section of CPI(M) workers who had fallen out with the party leadership over local issues. He entered the fray with their full support after severing ties with the party leadership, even giving up a temporary bank job arranged by the party.
UDF candidate P.K. Unais finished second with 250 votes, while LDF candidate P. Jayan secured 139 votes.
Despite senior CPI(M) leader campaigning and addressing public meetings in the area, the party failed to generate momentum in the Kara region, leading to the unexpected setback for the LDF.

title: Patients welcome introduction of the National Blood Transfusion Bill, 2025
summary: Thalassaemia patients support the National Blood Transfusion Bill, 2025, aiming for safer, standardized blood services across India.
content:
Thalassaemia patients have welcomed the introduction of the National Blood Transfusion Bill, 2025, in Parliament on Friday (December 12, 2025). The proposed legislation seeks to create a dedicated National Blood Transfusion Authority, set uniform national standards for the collection, testing, processing, storage, distribution, issuance and transfusion of blood and blood components, mandate registration of all blood centres, promote voluntary blood donation, and introduce strict penalties for unsafe or non-compliant practices.
“These provisions directly address long standing concerns faced by patients, caregivers, and clinicians due to fragmented regulation and inconsistent quality,” the Thalassemia Patients Advocacy Group (TPAG) said. It added that the reform offers hope for a safer, more accountable and more efficient blood ecosystem.
N.K. Ganguly, former Director General of the Indian Council of Medical Research, said, “Strengthening the governance of blood transfusion services is essential for ensuring safety and public trust. The proposed Bill provides a science-based framework to streamline standards and improve patient outcomes.”
Anubha Taneja Mukherjee, member secretary, TPAG, said, “For thousands of thalassaemia patients, blood is not a treatment. It is a lifeline. The Bill recognise the urgency of building a strong and unified national framework to ensure safe and equitable access to quality blood.”

title: UDF retains Kasaragod municipality, IUML wins 23 of 24 seats
summary: UDF retains Kasaragod municipality, with IUML winning 23 of 24 seats in the recent local body elections.
content:
The United Democratic Front (UDF) retained control of the Kasaragod municipal council, largely on the strength of the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), by winning 24 of the 39 wards in the local body elections.
Of the 24 seats secured by the UDF, 23 were won by the IUML. The National Democratic Alliance (NDA) saw its tally drop from 14 seats in the previous council to 12, while the Left Democratic Front (LDF) improved its presence from one seat to two, with one of the victories coming from an Independent candidate backed by the Left.
The Kasaragod municipality has remained a UDF stronghold since its formation, losing power only twice to the Left Democratic Front.
Although the BJP remains the second-largest party in the council, its strength declined this time. The NDA, which has been in the opposition for years, had set its sights on capturing power but failed to breach the UDF bastion.
The LDF, despite having a limited base in the municipality, fielded candidates in 25 wards in an attempt to assert its organisational strength. The Social Democratic Party of India (SDPI) also entered the fray by contesting in three wards- 1, 13, and 30, seeking to mark its presence. The UDF fielded candidates in 37 wards, including 24 from the IUML.
The UDF had also retained the municipality in the 2020 local body elections by winning 24 seats in the then 38-member council. Following that election, UDF councillor V.M. Muneer was elected chairman, though three councillors abstained from voting.
The post of municipal chairperson is reserved for women this term as well. Since the municipality’s formation, M. Ramannarai (1963) and S.J. Prasad (1995) have served as chairmen, while K.S. Sulaiman Haji (1970-94), former MP Hamidali Shamnad and T.E. Abdullah held the post in different periods. The chairperson’s post was earlier reserved for women in 2005 and 2015, when Beefathima Ibrahim served as administrator. In the previous council, V.M. Muneer headed the municipality in the first term, followed by Abbas Begum in the final term.

title: KSRTC launches ‘Accident Emergency Response Vehicles’ to improve bus accident and breakdown management
summary: KSRTC introduces Accident Emergency Response Vehicles to enhance bus accident management and provide swift support for stranded passengers.
content:
:
The Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) on Saturday (December 13, 2025) launched “Accident Emergency Response Vehicles” aimed at providing swift assistance during road accidents and vehicle breakdowns involving State-run buses. Initially, two Accident Emergency Response Vehicles will be deployed at central locations in Bengaluru and Mysuru.
Transport Minister Ramalinga Reddy flagged off a fleet of Accident Emergency Response Vehicles, which have the capacity to respond swiftly to bus accidents and breakdowns on major transport corridors.
According to Mr. Reddy, the specially equipped vehicles will function as mobile workshops, enabling technical teams to quickly reach stranded buses with the necessary tools, spare parts, and support to restore operations. “Initially, two vehicles have been stationed at central locations in Bengaluru and Mysuru. These units will cover high-traffic regions including Tumakuru, Kolar, Chikkaballapur, Mandya, and surrounding districts,” he said.
The Minister said the initiative was essential as buses operating from Kempegowda Bus Stand and Mysuru Road Bus Stand serve a wide network of intra-State and inter-State routes. “Frequent technical failures or accidents on busy stretches often lead to significant traffic congestion and inconvenience to commuters. The deployment of mobile workshop vehicles would allow staff to reach such sites without delay, clear obstructions, and minimise service disruptions,” Mr. Reddy added.
Transport Minister@RLR_BTMflags off Accident Emergency Response Vehicles in#Bengaluruto ensure quick response to bus accidents and breakdowns. The mobile workshop vehicles will reduce traffic congestion, assist staff and shift injured to hospitals.@THBengalurupic.twitter.com/EDVi8NovZ0
Apart from enabling on-site repairs, the new vehicles will also assist in emergency response. In the event of an accident, teams can provide immediate support to drivers and conductors and assist in shifting injured passengers to nearby hospitals when necessary.
Each vehicle costs ₹7.22 lakh. The KSRTC announced that 10 additional units will be inducted by the end of January 2026 and subsequently deployed across the remaining districts in a phased rollout to ensure Statewide coverage.
“These vehicles are light commercial vehicle (LCV) pickup chosen for their fuel efficiency, power output, and suitability for transporting equipment safely. The turbocharged, intercooled diesel engine complies with BS-VI emission standards. The High Side Deck design enables secure carriage of spare parts and repair tools vital for field operations,” a senior KSRTC official explained.

title: On its own, Welfare Party of India wins four seats in Mukkom
summary: Welfare Party of India secures four seats in Mukkom municipality, achieving victory independently amid local political tensions.
content:
Four candidates of the Welfare Party of India (WPI), a political party backed by the Jamaat-e-Islami Hind, registered an impressive victory in the Mukkom municipality without entering into any alliance with the major political fronts when the results of the local body elections were declared in Kozhikode district on Saturday.
This is significant because the United Democratic Front’s (UDF) alleged tie-up with the WPI was among the major issues raised by the Left Democratic Front (LDF) during the election campaign. In Mukkom municipality, however, the WPI had contested in six wards on its own after “alliance talks” with the UDF failed in view of certain local political compulsions.
In the 34-member municipal council, the WPI fielded its candidates in Kallurutty North, Kanakkuparamba, Mangalassery, Chennamangallur, Pulpparamba, and Pottassery wards. They won from Kanakkuparamba, Mangalassery, Chennamangallur, and Pulpparamba.
The winners are Mohammed Naseem, Shafeeque Madayi, V. Banooja, and Jaseela Azeez (Independent backed by the WPI), respectively. In the 2020 polls, the party had contested from four wards and won from Kanakkuparamba, Mangalassery, and Pulpparamba wards in “alliance” with the UDF.

title: UDF sweeps four Corporations, LDF reduced to one, BJP opens score
summary: UDF dominates Kerala local elections, winning four Corporations, while LDF drops to one and BJP secures its first win.
content:
The results of the local body elections in the six Corporations of Kerala signal a significant shift in the electoral fortunes of the three major fronts. It was almost a reversal of the trends witnessed five years ago as the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) won four Corporations, while the Left Democratic Front (LDF) which had won five of the six Corporations was reduced to just one Corporation. The most decisive shift was visible in the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation where the Bharatiya Janata Party-led NDA won, its first victory ever in a municipal corporation in the State.
Just like the trends visible in the BJP’s growth in other States, it has begun making its presence felt in most urban centres. The party now has a presence in all the Corporations in the State. The structured growth in Thiruvananthapuram Corporation, from 6 seats in 2010 to 50 seats this year, has aided it in capturing power. The LDF which has been in power for four decades could win only 29 wards, while the UDF improved its position from 10 to 19 wards, with 12 of these wins in LDF’s sitting wards.
The UDF recaptured power in the Kochi Corporation with a thumping win in 46 out of the 76 seats in the council. The LDF could only manage 20 seats, while the NDA improved its tally by one to six seats. In 2020, the LDF had managed to capture power in Kochi after winning 34 seats and the support of two independent candidates. While the UDF came close to its all-time highest tally of 48 in 2010, the LDF’s tally was worse than its tally of 24 that year.
The results in the Kozhikode Corporation came as a sort of relief for the LDF. Though it became the single biggest front with 34 seats, it still fell short of the majority number of 39 required in the 76 seats. The LDF’s seat share fell from 50 in 2020, while the UDF improved its tally from 18 to 26. The biggest difference this year has been the performance of the NDA, which went from just 1 seat in 2020 to 13 this year. Three independents have also won from the Corporation. The LDF’s Mayoral candidate C.P. Musafar Ahmed tasted defeat.
The UDF also staged a comeback in the Thrissur Corporation, which had witnessed a hung verdict in 2020. Though the BJP made a strong push to capture power, buoyed by Suresh Gopi’s victory in the Lok Sabha polls last year, it could improve its tally only by two seats from 6 to 8 seats. The UDF won in 33 seats, while the LDF was reduced to just 11 from 25 last time.
One of the most significant setbacks for the LDF was in the Kollam Corporation, which it has ruled for 25 uninterrupted years ever since the Corporation was formed in 2000. The UDF won 27 seats in the Corporation, two short of the majority mark. The LDF was reduced to 16 seats from the tally of 39 it secured in 2020. The NDA, which could manage to win in only one seat in the past two local body elections, won in 12 seats.

title: Mysuru’s SJCE-STEP turns 40, unveils deep-tech future
summary: SJCE-STEP celebrates 40 years of fostering innovation and entrepreneurship in Mysuru, unveiling plans for a deep-tech future.
content:
Sri Jayachamarajendra College of Engineering–Science & Technology Entrepreneurs Park (SJCE–STEP), one of the country’s earliest technology business incubators, is celebrating its 40th anniversary — a milestone that celebrates Mysuru’s rise as a major hub for innovation, deep-tech entrepreneurship, and technology-driven economic development.
Founded on December 13, 1985, with the support of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, and JSS Mahavidyapeetha, SJCE-STEP began as an experiment in nurturing technologists and innovators. Four decades later, it stands as an institution that has shaped many startups, accelerated industrial growth, and helped establish Mysuru as an innovation destination beyond Bengaluru, the incubator stated.
Suresh Bhojraj, director, Technical Education division, JSS Science and Technological University (STU), JSS Mahavidyapeetha, at a press conference here on December 13, said that STEP has been bridging education and enterprise for four decades and will drive future-ready talent and research linkages.
A.N. Santosh Kumar, Vice-Chancellor, JSS STU, underscored the growing integration between research, industry, and startup ecosystems, while Dhanraj, Registrar, JSS STU, emphasised the institution’s growing global partnerships. Nataraju, principal, SJCE, emphasised how innovation in universities is crucial for fostering creativity and driving economic growth. Manjunath Aradhya, Dean (Research), JSS STU, expressed the need to work on quantum computing, semiconductor, and natural language translation — in line with the national mission.
To mark the 40th anniversary, TBI 2.0, a next-generation deep-tech and AI innovation hub, is coming up with an investment of over ₹10 crore. K-TECH Common Infrastructure Facility (CIF), which is supported by the Department of Electronics, Information Technology-Biotechnology and Science & Technology, Government of Karnataka, in collaboration with Karnataka Digital Economy Mission, is coming up, a press release from SJCE-STEP said.
JSS Innovation and Research Park, spread over two lakh sq. ft and designed to scale research and development, innovation, testing, and commercialisation for startups and budding entrepreneurs, is also coming up in the campus. “These initiatives reflect a vision to support over a thousand startups in the coming years,” it further stated.
Shivashankar B., chief executive, SJCE-STEP, reaffirmed the commitment to deep-tech, AI, sustainability, semiconductors, and global collaboration. “Taking technology to the grassroots to bridge the digital gap and solve rural problems through innovation and rural incubation is our vision,” the release added.
It also explained that SJCE-STEP has proposed to build the next 1000+ startups for Viksit Bharat, encourage women-led entrepreneurship, build global research partnerships, and establish Mysuru as a competitive destination for deep-tech investments.

title: Kerala local body polls: UDF bucks the trend in Pathanamthitta, wins majority
summary: UDF achieves a historic majority in Pathanamthitta local body polls, winning key panchayats and municipalities from LDF.
content:
Defying a long-standing political pattern in the district, the United Democratic Front (UDF) has scored a decisive breakthrough in Pathanamthitta, wresting control of the district panchayat and a majority of local bodies from the Left Democratic Front (LDF).
The Congress-led coalition, carrying  forward its momentum from last year’s Lok Sabha elections, has won a clear majority in the district panchayat, besides securing control of 34 grama panchayats and seven block panchayats. The UDF also registered significant gains in the municipal segment winning three municipalities, including two that were earlier held by the LDF.
In the 16-member district panchayat, the UDF won a comfortable majority with 12 seats, while the LDF’s tally fell sharply to five from 12 in the previous election. Among the notable winners was Sreenadevi Kunjamma, who switched allegiance from the Communist Party of India (CPI) to the Congress at the eleventh hour and contested as a UDF candidate from the Pallickal division.
Of the four municipalities in the district, the UDF emerged ahead in Pathanamthitta, Thiruvalla and Adoor. However, in Thiruvalla, the coalition fell short of securing a clear majority. The Bharatiya Janata Party-led National Democratic Alliance (BJP-NDA), meanwhile, lost the Pandalam municipality where it had created history in 2020 by winning a simple majority. This time, the LDF took the lead with 14 seats, closely followed by the UDF with 11, while the NDA was restricted to nine seats.
At the same time, the NDA put up a strong performance in the Thiruvalla municipality, winning seven seats.
In the grama panchayat segment, the UDF won 34 of the 53 panchayats in the district, a sharp rise from its previous tally. The LDF was confined to 11 panchayats, down from 23 last time, while the NDA emerged victorious in four. The remaining four panchayats returned a hung verdict.
The UDF also tightened its grip on the block panchayats, winning seven of the eight blocks in the district, with Konni being the lone exception. The LDF retained only one block panchayat.
The BJP won six seats overall, including three in Pandalam and one each in Mallappally, Koipuram and Parakkodu, apart from securing 125 grama panchayat wards across the district.

title: House panel recommends 5-day jail term for 4 journalists for defaming MLC Mitkari
summary: Maharashtra panel proposes five-day jail term for four journalists accused of defaming MLC Amol Mitkari through false reporting.
content:
A Special Privileges Committee of the Maharashtra legislative council has recommended a five-day jail sentence for four journalists for defaming member Amol Mitkari by running “false and fabricated” news against him.
Prasad Lad, chairman of the committee, informed the Upper House of the State legislature on Saturday (December 13, 2025) that a YouTube channel named ‘Satya Ladha’ had broadcast fabricated and false reports against Mitkari to tarnish his public image.
Mr. Mitkari had filed a breach of privilege motion against the four Akola-based journalists — Ganesh Sonawane, Harshada Sonawane, Amol Nandurkar, Ankush Gawande — and Satya Ladha, editor Satish Deshmukh.
Mr. Lad informed the council that the Special Privileges Committee conducted an inquiry into the complaint and concluded that Ganesh Sonawane, Harshada Sonawane, Amol Nandurkar and Ankush Gawande were responsible for broadcasting defamatory and misleading material.
The committee recommended no action against editor Satish Deshmukh, as he has submitted a written apology, said Mr. Lad.
The panel has proposed that the four journalists be sentenced to five days’ imprisonment.
The House panel has suggested that the four journalists be punished during the ongoing winter session of the State legislature, or, if that is not possible, the recommendation must be implemented in the next session.

title: List of provisionally admitted candidates available on APPSC website
summary: APPSC lists provisionally admitted candidates for lecturer posts; certificate verification scheduled from December 29 to 31, 2025.
content:
The Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission (APPSC) has made available on its website www.psc.ap.gov.in the list of candidates provisionally admitted for verification of original certificates for the post of lecturers in Government Polytechnic Colleges (Engineering and Non-Engineering) in A.P. Technical Education Service, on the basis of written examination (CBT) held from July 15, 2025 to July 22, 2025.
A statement issued by the Commission said verification of the original certificates would be held from December 29, 2025, to December 31, 2025, at 9.30 a.m. in the APPSC office opposite Indira Gandhi Municipal Stadium in Vijayawada. The verification process would be followed by a Computer Proficiency Test (CPT) the same day. The commission said a detailed schedule for verification of certificates would be published soon.

title: Andhra Pradesh stands first in energy conservation at the national level
summary: Andhra Pradesh secures first place in national energy conservation for the fourth year, showcasing effective energy efficiency initiatives.
content:
Andhra Pradesh won the first prize in Group-II — States with total final energy consumption between 5 and 15 Million Tonnes of Oil Equivalent (Mtoe) — of the National Energy Conservation Awards for the 4th consecutive year, according to a press release by Chief Secretary K. Vijayanand.
He said that the State got the recognition for its commitment and the results achieved by it in implementing energy conservation and efficiency schemes in buildings, industry, municipal, agriculture, DISCOMs and transport sectors.
Andhra Pradesh emerged as the top performer by scoring 89.25 points in the State Energy Efficiency Index (SEEI) - 2025 against 87.25 in the SEEI–2024.
APSPDCL CMD L. Sivasankar was nominated to receive the award on behalf of the AP State Energy Conservation Mission (AP-SECM) from President Droupadi Murmu, at Vigyan Bhavan in New Delhi on December 14 (National Energy Conservation Day).
The Chief Secretary said Andhra Pradesh stood at the forefront at the national level in executing its energy conservation strategy through comprehensive, scalable, and impactful programmes, and by ensuring cooperation between all the government departments concerned, consumers, and stakeholders.
The government’s key initiatives towards achieving the goals include the Integrated Clean Energy Policy, the AP Industrial Development Policy 4.0 (2024–29) and sector-specific policies for MSMEs, electronics, and food processing.
Significant advancements were made in enforcing the Energy Conservation Building Code (ECBC), implementing energy efficiency projects in schools, hospitals and ITI colleges, and introducing advanced technologies in MSMEs, Mr. Vijayanand added.
In her message, AP-Genco MD and SECM CEO S. Nagalakshmi thanked  BEE for its support and collaboration, while acknowledging the contributions of Industries, Transport, Housing and Roads & Buildings departments and the DISCOMs.

title: Students advised to embrace challenges
summary: Students encouraged to embrace challenges and adopt a growth mindset for lasting success, as highlighted in a guest lecture.
content:
Motivation provides the initial spark to start a task or goal, but discipline is the consistent effort and habit that sustains you, carrying you through challenges and building long-term success when feelings fade, said faculty member at the University of Massachusetts Chaerin Kim.
Delivering a guest lecture titled ‘Professional Development, Mental Focus and Discipline to be Global Leaders’, organised by the Department of Science and Humanities at Siddhartha Deemed University on Friday (December 12), Ms. Kim said motivation is the fuel, while discipline is the engine and roadmap, turning initial excitement into real, lasting achievement.
She advised the students to shift from a fixed mindset (believing abilities are static) to a growth mindset (believing abilities develop with effort) and encouraged them to embrace challenges, see effort as key, learn from failure as a chance to improve, and value strategies over innate talent, fostering resilience and higher achievement.
Vice-chancellor P. Venkateswara Rao, Pro vice-chancellor A.V. Ratna Prasad, registrar M. Ravichand and dean D. Venkat Rao were present.

title: Students should focus on problem-driven learning: experts
summary: Experts advocate for problem-driven learning in MBA programs, emphasizing real-world experiences over rote learning for career success.
content:
Students should focus on problem-driven learning and develop the ability to deal with ambiguity and complexity on the ground, experts suggested at a webinar on ‘Beyond the Classroom: The Real MBA Experience’.
The webinar, presented by Vellore Institute of Technology in collaboration withThe HinduEducation Plus under its Career Path series, sought to explain how value-addition comes from doing on-site MBA courses from good B-schools, such as VIT and others. While upscaling through pedagogy is important, rote learning is passe, and practical and real world learning outside the classroom shapes the MBA journey better and impacts students’ career prospects, the speakers contended.
Simulation-based learning and industry project-based courses have the most profound impact on students, leading them to critical thinking, confidence building, ethical leadership, and responsible management, said Mary Cherian, Dean of Business School at VIT. Students have to use every opportunity to develop new knowledge and skills and make themselves industry-ready, she added.
Anwar Sadad, co-founder, Olive Ridley, a B2B hygiene solutions company, an alumni of the VIT Business School, said the programme taught him about “price, promotion, product, and place”. But real-time experiences in later years taught him to add three more ‘P’s — Patience, Perseverance, and Problem-solving. “These are the three qualities every industry expects of a business student,” he added.
S. Sasikumar, director (Admissions), and professor (higher academic grade), guided the participants through the application-to-admission process at VIT and also walked them through the various overseas partnerships available. “To maximise success in the MBA programme, you cannot afford to be a loner. The campus environment, peers, and professors accelerate your learning,” he added.
For the full webinar, visit: https://newsth.live/THVITYT

title: KTR unveils QR code-embedded shawl showcasing Telangana’s heritage, projects
summary: KTR unveils QR code-embedded shawl showcasing Telangana’s heritage, projects
content:
HYDERABAD
Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) working president and former Minister K.T. Rama Rao unveiled a specially-designed handloom shawl embedded with a QR code at his Nandi Nagar residence on Saturday.
The shawl, created by noted weaver and Chenetha Kala Ratna awardee Nalla Vijay Kumar from Sircilla, features a scannable QR code that presents Telangana’s history, major temples, iconic structures, traditions and key development initiatives undertaken during the previous BRS government led by K. Chandrasekhar Rao, including Mission Bhagiratha and the Kaleshwaram Lift Irrigation Project (KLIP).
The QR code is described as “pogu bandham to phone bandham” (Relationship between thread and phone network), enabling users to access detailed information on the State’s cultural heritage and development milestones. Mr. Vijay Kumar said the shawl took 15 days to complete.
Mr. Rama Rao appreciated the weaver for his craftsmanship and creativity, stating that the unique handloom creation effectively reflected the spirit and achievements of Telangana. “It will be presented to KCR,” KTR added.
Mr. Vijay Kumar, known for his innovative weaving, had earlier crafted a silk and zari shawl embedded with a QR code highlighting the achievements of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Carrying forward his family’s legacy, he is the son of Nalla Parandhamulu, the first weaver to create a silk saree that could fit inside a matchbox.
His earlier creations include sarees that can pass through a needle’s eye or a finger ring, a colour-changing “chameleon” saree and a fragrant silk saree. He had also presented Prime Minister Modi with a gold “Operation Sindoor” shawl woven by him.

title: Making brain death determination a standard of care in ICUs
summary: Transforming brain death determination into a standard ICU practice could enhance organ donation processes and clinician confidence in India.
content:
Two weeks ago, disposing off a petition filed by the  Indian Society of Organ Transplantation, seeking a uniform national framework to ensure equity, access and efficiency in organ donation and transplantation across India, the Supreme Court issued a series of directives to the Centre, so that eventually,  a model national organ allocation policy can be framed.
One of the directives suggested that the government consider amending Form 4 and 4A of the Registration of Births and Deaths Rules 1999 so that a new column be added to indicate whether the deceased was a case of brain stem death and whether the option of organ donation was given to the family.
This would make brain death certification a normal, non-negotiable definition of death, just as cardiac death, thereby opening up the possibility that brain death declaration and possible organ donation becomes a standard hospital procedure, not a transplant-driven activity.
Kerala became the first State towards this when in 2020, it took the bold step of delinking brain death certification and organ donation.
In India, brain death has been defined only in connection with organ donation, in the Transplantation of Human Organs Act, 1994. Thus clinicians perceived brain death certification as a procedure that is done solely to aid organ donation. Doctors had no clarity on what they should do if, after brain death certification, the family refused the option of organ donation.
Putting an end to the ethical dilemma of clinicians, the GO issued by Kerala set forth parameters for brain death certification in ICUs and stated that once a patient has been pronounced brain-dead as per the protocol, all treatment, including cardio-respiratory support should be discontinued.
Organ donation counselling would come as a sequel to brain death certification, leaving the final decision on organ donation to families.
It was hoped that this clarification and legal consent would make clinicians more proactive and fearless about brain death certification. But nothing has changed in the last five years and doctors continue to shy away from the process.
Brain death certification and deceased donation continues to be an activity that happens in Kerala only when some well-informed families demand that the organs of their loved one be donated and make a push for it.
“Brain death certification is not a concept that the doctors of the day are very familiar with, given that the topic is not something that was dealt with during their undergraduate studies. That knowledge gap seems to persist, so that brain death certification, which is the standard of care across the globe, continues to be alien to them,” a senior medical professional feels.
Neurological death determination is a resource as well as knowledge-intensive process and despite the rigorous training they received, most doctors are still not confident about handling the process of brain death determination.
“At least 400 doctors in the State have been given intensive training in the brain death determination and certification process. But sad enough, none of them are taking proactive steps to make brain death determination a standard of care. Brain death determination has to be a zero-error process and that level of self confidence is rarely seen amongst our doctors,” says Noble Gracious, Executive Director of Kerala State Organ and Tissue  Transplantation Organisation (K-SOTTO).
He feels that it is this intense scrutiny over the process and the pressure  that there is no room for error that seems to be dissuading doctors from doing brain death determination.
“Front-runner nations in organ donation, such as the U.S. and Spain, developed their organ transplant programme over a period of 30 years, with the doctors undergoing continuous, rigorous  hands-on training on various scenarios before brain death determination became a practice in their ICUs. That is a huge learning curve which will take much time and practice to master and we need to be patient,” says Dr. Gracious.
Which is why the State needs to take a re-look at its organ transplantation scene.
Kerala’s unique challenges standing in the way of organ donation should be analysed and the confidence of the medical community in the process of brain death determination should be built through continuous training and system support, so that it becomes a routine practice in the State’s ICUs.

title: Teachers will play pivotal role in making India a global leader, says APSCHE chief
summary: Teachers are crucial for India's global leadership by 2047, emphasises APSCHE chief at educational event in Vijayawada.
content:
Andhra Pradesh State Council of Higher Education (APSCHE) chairperson K. Madhu Murthy on Saturday (December 13) said teachers and the education system will play a decisive role in making India a global leader by 2047.
Speaking at the inaugural session of a two-day Andhra Pradesh Prantha Abhyasa Varga-2025, organised by Akhila Bharatiya Rashtriya Saikshik Mahasabha (ABRSM) at K.L. Deemed to be University, Mr. Murthy said the National Education Policy (NEP-2020), introduced under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the Centre, aimed at aligning the education system with the nation’s developmental needs in sectors such as industry, agriculture, housing, health and employment generation, while also working towards poverty eradication.
He emphasised that India’s ancient knowledge systems and rich heritage must be integrated into modern education to strengthen the system further. Mr. Murthy noted that NEP-2020 will play a vital role in achieving the goals of Viksit Bharat and Swarna Andhra.
National joint organising secretary of ABRSM G. Lakshman said the Mahasabha was a leading teachers’ organisation with nearly 15 lakh members ranging from primary to higher education institutions. He stressed that the education system must progress in harmony with India’s culture, traditions, values and humanity to enable the nation to emerge as a world leader.
Pro-chancellor of KL University Rajasekhar Rao urged teachers across the country to imbibe a strong national spirit, continuously enhance their subject expertise and guide students towards academic excellence.
Nearly 200 faculty members from Degree, Engineering and Intermediate colleges, state and Central universities, and other higher educational institutions participated in the event.
ABRSM State president Y.V. Rami Reddy presided over the session, while ABRSM State general secretary D.S.V.S. Balasubramaniam and State Mahila Pramukh Sandhya Adhuri were also present.

title: TDP leader denies ‘coercion’ of YSRCP corporators ahead of Nellore Mayor election
summary: TDP leader Giridhar Reddy denies YSRCP's coercion claims ahead of the Nellore Mayor election, emphasizing action over rhetoric.
content:
Kotamreddy Giridhar Reddy, TDP leader and brother of Nellore Rural MLA Kotamreddy Sridhar Reddy, on Saturday, said that the party would demonstrate its strength in the Nellore Municipal Corporation elections scheduled for December 18.
Speaking to the media at Kanipakam here, following prayers at Varasiddhi Vinayaka Swamy temple along with a group of corporators, Mr. Giridhar Reddy dismissed allegations by YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) leaders that the TDP was coercing corporators to secure support in the mayoral election.
The TDP leader said the party believed in action rather than rhetoric and would not indulge in claims on who would become the Mayor. “We will show our strength through our work. The outcome will be evident on the day of the election,” he said.
Rejecting claims that YSRCP corporators were brought to Kanipakam to be forced to take oaths due to inadequate support for the mayoral election, he termed the allegations ‘baseless’. He added that the TDP did not require oaths or assurances to secure support.

title: ‘Clarity of purpose transforms dreams into reality’
summary: Seetarama Kotagiri emphasizes clarity of purpose in transforming dreams into reality during KLE Technological University's convocation address.
content:
Chief Executive Officer of Magna International, Seetarama (Swamy) Kotagiri has urged students to keep asking ‘what’s next?’, because it is the clarity of purpose that transforms dreams into reality.
An alumnus of BVB College of Engineering and Technology (now KLE Technological University), Mr. Seetarama (Swamy) Kotagiri was delivering the convocation address at the seventh convocation of KLE Technological University at Dr. Prabhakar Kore Sports Arena in Hubballi on Saturday.
Mr. Seetarama, who took a stroll down memory lane, told the graduating students that as they were stepping into a world filled with incredible opportunities and real challenges, they would require resilience, creativity, humility, and courage.
He asked them to remember five simple things to achieve their goals. “You don’t need perfect conditions, you just need to start. Courage will take you further than certainty. Keep learning and keep asking ‘why?’ as curiosity always creates opportunity. Surround yourself with people who make you better. Choose people who lift you, challenge you, and ground you. Find a way to leave every place better than you found it,” he said.
Mr. Seetarama told the graduating candidates to make improvements through small gestures and also remember that one did not have to solve everything at once. “Ask yourself a simple question like what can I make better today? You will be amazed by where life takes you,” he said.
Quoting Robert Frost’s famous poem ‘The Road Not Taken’, he said: “Every meaningful journey in life involves choosing a road that others may overlook. It takes courage to step into the unknown. When you do, you not only shape your own future but open new paths for those who come after you”.
He advised them to have personal, professional, family and societal goals to lead a balanced and meaningful life.
Chancellor of KLE Technological University and chairman of KLE Society Prabhakar Kore declared the convocation open and conferred various degrees. Vice-Chancellor Prakash Tewari presented a brief report of the university highlighting its achievements.
Pro Chancellor Ashok Shettar, Registrar Basavaraj Anami, Prof. B.L. Desai, Prof. B.B. Kottur Shettar and heads of various departments, members of the Board of Governors, Executive Council and Academic Council, senior faculty members were present.
In all, 21 gold medals, including 15 for graduates and six for postgraduates; silver medals for 15 graduates and seven postgraduates, along with the Dr. S.S. Bhavikatti Gold Medal for topper in Civil Department were presented. A total of 2,466 students were awarded their degrees in engineering sciences, law, computer application, business administration and fashion and apparel design.

title: LDF improves show to take Neyyattinkara
summary: The Left Democratic Front (LDF) swept the Neyyattinkara municipality in the local body elections, winning 25 of the 46 seats and one more than the required majority of 24.
content:
The Left Democratic Front (LDF) swept the Neyyattinkara municipality in the local body elections, winning 25 of the 46 seats and one more than the required majority of 24.
The LDF improved its performance significantly from that in 2020 when it won 18 seats, just one more than the 17 for the United Democratic Front (UDF) (in the then 44-member municipality).
For the UDF, it was a dismal show this time, with its tally slipping to 12, the same as that in 2015. The UDF had last come to power in the municipality in 2010.
The National Democratic Alliance (NDA) secured seven seats, two less than that in 2020. It could not make the sort of strides it had in 2020 when the NDA tally increased to nine from five in 2015.
Independents won in two wards – Thozhukkal and Amaravila.
The LDF and the NDA, respectively, split the two new wards of Therannoor and Chemmanthattu.
The LDF also failed to retain its sitting seats of Aaralummoodu, Pallivilakam, and Chundavila, losing them to the UDF.
However, it managed to snatch Vadakode, Chaikottukonam, Pullamala, and Brahmamcode from the UDF.
The LDF also took away Aalampotta, Plavila, Maruthathoor, Rameswaram, and Athiyannoor from the BJP.
The UDF lost Mullaravila, Punnakkadu, and Perumpazhathoor to the NDA.
In Thozhukkal, an Independent won against the Congress candidate.
Former municipal chairperson W.R. Heeba who contested the polls again after a gap of five years from Thavaravila defeated Ashalatha S. of the BJP by a margin of 106 votes.
LDF heavyweight and former municipal vice chairperson K.K. Shibu who contested from Kavalakulam despite initial doubts over his candidacy owing to the CPI(M) policy of not fielding a candidate more than twice consecutively did not let the front down, coasting to a comfortable win.
P. Rajan, another prominent name, however, lost to S.J. Prabin of the Congress. R.V. Vijayabose defeated the UDF candidate in Olathanni ward.
The Congress will need to examine if the sexual harassment controversy surrounding District Congress Committee general secretary Jose Franklin had an impact on its fortunes.
Shibu Raj Krishna, who was leader of the BJP in the 2020 council, however, fell to Aji R. of the LDF in Chaikottukonam.
NGO Sangh former general secretary S.K. Jayakumar failed to get past LDF candidate Sureshkumar B. in Panangattukari.
Mr. Krishna’s sister M. Kala also lost in Narayanapuram ward.
The NDA retained Koottapana ward where Supriya Mahesh, wife of N. Mahesan Nair who won the seat in 2020, won against Anitha K. of the Congress.
Sangeetha Prasad, sister of Manchathala Suresh who won from Aalummoodu in 2020, bagged the seat defeating Aarabhi A. Padman, daughter of former council chairman K.R. Padmakumar.
D. Soumya who had won on the LDF ticket in Kavalakulam in 2020 but ran afoul of the party came third in Athazhamangalam where she contested as an independent.
However, Biju T.S. who was contesting as an Independent in Amaravila after differences with the CPI(M) won without any trouble.

title: GMC focuses on long-pending road widening works at Brindavan Gardens
summary: GMC Mayor directs swift action on long-delayed road widening at Brindavan Gardens to enhance traffic flow and connectivity.
content:
Directing the city planning officials to expedite the long-pending road widening works on Brindavan Gardens Main Road, Guntur Municipal Corporation Mayor Kovelamudi Ravindra instructed them to remove encroachments along the stretch to ease traffic and improve connectivity in the city.
The Mayor, accompanied by Municipal Commissioner Puli Srinivasulu, inspected Brindavan Gardens and Lakshmipuram Main Roads and reviewed the progress of ongoing and proposed works on Saturday. During the inspection, he issued clear instructions to town planning and engineering officials on timelines and execution.
Speaking on the occasion, the Mayor said the widening of Brindavan Gardens Main Road had remained pending for several years and had finally taken shape during the present coalition government’s tenure. He stressed that the project should be completed strictly as per the approved plan and asserted that encroachments along the road must be cleared without delay.
The Commissioner said permissions had already been granted for the construction of drains on both sides of the connecting road from Brindavan Gardens Centre to Vidhya Nagar Main Road. He instructed engineering officials to widen the road to 80 feet first, followed by the construction of drains and laying of a new road. He also directed town planning officials to remove encroachments along Lakshmipuram and Koritepadu Main Roads, particularly near drainage lines.

title: Telangana GP Polls-2025 second phase polling on Sunday
summary: Telangana's second phase of Gram Panchayat Elections-2025 takes place on December 14, featuring 3,911 Sarpanch and 29,917 Ward Member posts.
content:
The polls to the second phase ofTelangana Gram Panchayat Elections-2025would be held on Sunday (December 14, 2025). The first phase polls were held on Thursday and 3,834 Sarpanches, 27,346 Ward Members and 3,347 Up Sarpanches were elected. While 56,19,430 were registered voters, 45,15,141 exercised their franchise registered 84.28% turnout.
While 4331 Gram Panchayats (GP) were notified under the second phase, 415 Sarpanches were elected unanimously and no nominations were received for five. This leads to polls in 3911 GPs. The voting begins at 7 a.m. and concludes at 1.00 p.m. The counting would begin from 2.00 p.m. Results would be out from the early evening.
In the second phase, 57.22 lakh voters (29.26 lakh female and 27.96 lakh male) would decide the fate of 12,782 candidates contesting for 3,911 Sarpanch posts and 71,071 for 29,917 Ward Member posts.
Nagarkurnool Collector Badavath Santhosh interacting with polling staff
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                BY ARRANGEMENT
Meanwhile, Telangana State Election Commission has directed the Nalgonda Collector (District Election Authority) to conduct an iniquity into an issue where officers on election duty in Chinnakaparthi Gram Panchayat in Chityal mandal ‘were negligent in safe storage of election materials’ and take action.
Polling material at a distribution centre in Nagarkurnool district
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                BY ARRANGEMENT
Wanaparthy Collector Adarsh Surabhi on Friday asked the polling staff to allow only the contesting candidate or the candidate’s agent to the counting centre on the day of vote counting and they should not be allowed to take their phones. Reports of polling should be sent at 9 a.m., 11 a.m. and 1 p.m.
The Collectors of various districts and General Observers inspected polling material distribution centres on Saturday. Nagarkurnool Collector Badavath Santosh said that action would be taken against staff who are absent from polling duties; he issued directions to send names of the staff — on unauthorized absence — for suspension. Mahabubnagar Collector Viziendira Boyi distribution centre at Zilla Parishad High School in Koukuntla Mandal to check the arrangements for polling material.

title: LDF’s uninterrupted 25-year reign ends in Kollam Corporation
summary: UDF's victory in Kollam Corporation ends LDF's 25-year rule, marking a significant political shift in Kerala's local elections.
content:
The Kollam Corporation recorded one of the most definitive and surprising outcomes of the 2025 Kerala local body elections as the United Democratic Front (UDF) achieved a surprising sweep ending the uninterrupted 25-year reign of the Left Democratic Front (LDF) in its stronghold.
Securing 27 divisions in the 56-member council, the UDF could wrest control of the Corporation, marking a major political recovery. This unprecedented victory, a massive turnaround from the LDF’s overwhelming majority in 2020, confirms a paradigm shift in urban voter sentiment and serves as a major boost for the UDF ahead of upcoming Assembly elections.
Basically, the results reflect the changing political map of Kollam, with the UDF taking power, the LDF suffering a major setback, and the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) striding forward with notable gains.
While the LDF plummeted from a near-two-thirds majority of 39 seats in 2020 to just 16 seats in 2025, UDF’s jump from 9 to 27 seats is a remarkable turnaround. Compounding the LDF’s loss, the NDA doubled its tally to 12 seats, while the defeat of two former Mayors, Communist Party of India (CPI)’s Honey Benjamin (Vadakkumbhagam) and Communist Party of India (Marxist)’s [CPI(M)] V. Rajendrababu (Uliyakovil), underscored the deep anti-incumbency wave that swept the Corporation. LDF’s loss signals a massive rejection of the incumbent administration and dissatisfaction over civic issues.
The polls also saw the NDA cementing its status as a major political force in the Kollam Corporation, winning 12 seats, only four less than the LDF’s final tally, and ushering in a truly tri-polar political scene. The most telling sign of the NDA’s surge and the LDF’s vulnerability was that the NDA held the second position in the overall count during the initial hours of counting. The increase in the NDA’s vote share and seat count undoubtedly contributed to the LDF’s colossal losses.

title: Congress quashes Gopinathan’s challenge in Peringottukurissi, yet misses majority
summary: The Congress put to rest the challenge posed by dissident leader and former District Congress Committee (DCC) president A.V. Gopinathan by decisively defeating him in Peringottukurissi panchayat.
content:
The Congress put to rest the challenge posed by dissident leader and former District Congress Committee (DCC) president A.V. Gopinathan by decisively defeating him in Peringottukurissi panchayat.
However, the Congress’ victory over Mr. Gopinathan proved to be a pyrrhic one, as the party lost several crucial seats to a joint front formed by Mr. Gopinathan’s Independent Democratic Front (IDF) and the Left Democratic Front (LDF).
With seven seats in the 18-member panchayat council, the Congress remains three short of a majority. The LDF secured five seats, the IDF four, and the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) two, making the NDA’s position crucial in Peringottukurissi.
Congress candidate K.R. Ratheesh defeated Mr. Gopinathan by 134 votes in the Bemmanniyur ward. The LDF contested 12 seats and won five, while the IDF contested six and secured four, though it lost its skipper. Even together, the IDF–LDF combine has only nine seats, falling one short of a majority.
In the 2020 civic body elections, Mr. Gopinathan remained with the Congress despite having drifted away from the party. In that election, the UDF secured 11 seats, while the LDF won five.
Mr. Gopinathan’s attempt to cripple the Congress by aligning with the CPI(M) backfired with his defeat, marking the first electoral setback of his political career.
Mr. Gopinathan served as president of the Peringottukurissi grama panchayat for 25 years. He also holds the distinction of being the only Congress candidate to win from the Alathur Assembly constituency in its 68-year history, having secured a victory there in 1991 by a margin of 338 votes.
Though Mr. Gopinathan had kept his distance from the Congress since 2009, he formally broke away from the party after being denied an Assembly seat in 2021. He publicly declared his exit in 2023 when he participated in the Nava Kerala Sadas led by Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan.
Mr. Gopinathan had been the face of the Congress’s I-group in the district. His defeat has boosted the Congress’s confidence in Peringottukurissi, while simultaneously dealing a major setback to the CPI(M) in the area.

title: UDF wrests control of Narath, Kunnothuparamba panchayats
summary: UDF gains control of Narath and Kunnothuparamba panchayats, winning a majority in local body elections against LDF.
content:
The United Democratic Front (UDF) has wrested control of the Narath grama panchayat from the Left Democratic Front (LDF), securing a clear majority in the 18-member local body. The UDF won 11 seats, comfortably crossing the majority mark of nine, while the LDF was restricted to seven seats.
Although the LDF led in the initial rounds of counting, the UDF gained momentum in the later stages and maintained its lead till the end.  Of the 11 seats won by the UDF, the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) secured eight, while the Congress won three.
The UDF also wrested control of the Kunnothuparamba grama panchayat from the LDF in the local body elections. Of the total wards, the UDF secured victories in 11, while the LDF won nine and the NDA emerged victorious in three wards.
Earlier, LDF governed the panchayat with a strength of 10, while UDF had eight and NDA had three in the council.

title: Book exploring the inner workings of tax administration in India released
summary: Discover the insights of India's tax administration in Pratap Singh's memoir-style book, revealing transformative leadership and citizen-centric reforms.
content:
A book delineating the inner workings of the Indian tax administration, authored in the memoir style by Pratap Singh, Director-General of Income Tax (Investigation), Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, was released here on Friday.
While the book begins with the author’s life in the countryside, it delves into the internal mechanisms and processes within the Indian Revenue Service and fanning out to a few episodes in the author’s career like the Gurgaon model, where tax collections were tripled in three years after the department carried out experiments on how to make taxes more inclusive, acceptable, and involve the community as a whole.
Releasing the book, former National Security Advisor and former Governor of West Bengal M.K.
