Narayanan said Mr. Singh was able to rise above the mundane and produce a treatise that he regarded as thought leadership in the field of tax administration. “How does thought leadership come into tax administration, that is the gulf that Mr. Singh has managed to bridge,” he said.
“There is a thread that runs through the book about India, a nation intent on regaining its past glory so as to take its appointed place in the committee of nations,” Mr. Narayanan observed, adding, “What makes this book special is that it demonstrates how an elite, technical education can translate into refining public service leadership, including in fields such as revenue generation, also how tax administration should be simply refined in a way that it becomes more citizen centric.”
Amitabh Kant, former G20 Sherpa of India and former CEO of NITI Aayog, said each chapter in the book captured not just the places where the author was posted but also the various phases in the evolution of tax administration and institutions. “You see how technology reforms and data systems slowly transform an old-styled tax system into a modern, data-driven, and citizen friendly organisation,” he added.
Shankar Jiwal, former Tamil Nadu Director-General of Police, A.K. Viswanathan, former Commissioner of the Greater Chennai Police, Shreesh Chandra, founder-director, OakBridge Publishing, and Mr. Singh, and his wife Sadhana Singh also spoke.

title: ‘Heritage Treasure Hunt’ for Poorna Chethana School students and parents to be held on December 21
summary: Join the Mysuru Heritage Treasure Hunt on December 21 for Poorna Chethana School students and parents, celebrating culture and teamwork.
content:
The Poorna Chethana School has organised ‘Mysuru Heritage Treasure Hunt’ for students and their parents on December 21. The event will also feature a heritage flash mob, through which students will showcase Mysuru’s culture and traditions.
The programme aims to instil cultural awareness among children while strengthening the parent-child bond. Designed for children below 16 years, the event will begin at 7 a.m. at Sri Kote Anjaneya Swamy Temple. The competition will conclude at the same venue.
Each participating team will be provided with a special treasure kit containing 10 clues. A press release explained that teams will have to visit historical and heritage locations in Mysuru city and solve the clues.
The winning teams will receive cash prizes of ₹10,000, ₹7,500, and ₹5,000, along with trophies. All participating teams will be awarded certificates. For registration, participants can send a WhatsApp message to 7204836513, the release added.

title: UDF returns to power in Kannur Corporation
summary: UDF wins a decisive majority in Kannur Corporation, defeating LDF and celebrating a significant electoral victory.
content:
Delivering a major setback to the Left Democratic Front (LDF), the United Democratic Front (UDF) secured a clear majority in the Kannur Corporation by winning 36 of the 56 wards.
In the Kannur Corporation, where 1,35,780 of the total 1,93,079 voters cast their vote, the LDF finished a distant second with 14 seats, while the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) won four seats. Besides retaining the Pallikunnu ward, the NDA also won Kokkenpara, Thulicheri and Temple wards. The Congress lost the Thulicheri and Temple wards to the BJP.
Compared to the previous election, the UDF improved its tally from 34 to 36 seats, while the LDF’s strength fell from 19 to 15 seats. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) increased its representation by three seats. The Social Democratic Party of India (SDPI) also secured one seat from the Arakkal ward.
Several prominent LDF leaders suffered defeats. P.K. Ragesh lost from Panikkara, former State Sports Council president O.K. Vineesh was defeated in Thalikkavu, and former standing committee chairperson K.P. Sabira lost from Arakkal.
Meanwhile, three rebel candidates who contested against the UDF in Payyambalam (K.N. Bindu), Varam (K.V. Riyas) and Adikadalayi (V. Muhammadali) wards were defeated, further consolidating the UDF’s position in the Corporation.
Following the victory, UDF workers celebrated across key parts of the city, bursting firecrackers and holding victory marches. UDF convener P.T. Mathew, DCC president Martin George, IUML district president Abdul Kareem Cheleri, and former Mayor Muslih Madathil led a victory procession in an open vehicle along with the elected candidates, greeting the public. Party workers participated in large numbers, carrying flags and banners.

title: Cong-backed candidates win 45 GPs in Sangareddy constituency, felicitated
summary: Cong-backed candidates win 45 GPs in Sangareddy constituency, felicitated
content:
SANGAREDDY
District Congress Committee (DCC) president and Telangana Government Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (TGIIC) chairperson T. Nirmala Jagga Reddy on Saturday felicitated newly elected Sarpanches, ward members and Upa-Sarpanches who secured victories in the Sangareddy Assembly constituency at a programme held at a constituency-level meeting in Sangareddy.
Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) working president T. Jagga Reddy also felicitated Congress candidates who were defeated in the elections, acknowledging their efforts and commitment in strengthening the party at the grassroots level. It said that Congress-backed candidates had won in 45 Gram Panchayats in the constituency.
Addressing the gathering, Mr. Jagga Reddy said the victories were achieved through unity, strength and dedication, despite his absence from the campaign.
Clarifying the party’s stand, Mr. Jagga Reddy said there would be no entry into the Congress for candidates who contested and won as rebels. However, he said independent candidates who emerged victorious could join the party after a decision by the Block Congress and Mandal Congress leadership.
On the occasion, he announced that Masku Alavani Narasimha Reddy, who was defeated in the Kondapur sarpanch election, would be appointed as chairman of the Sadashivapet Market Committee.

title: Maghi Sambhrama highlights traditional winter flavours
summary: Experience Mysuru's Maghi Sambhrama, celebrating traditional winter flavors and culinary delights, showcasing unique crops and dishes.
content:
The two-day Maghi Sambhrama, inaugurated in the city on December 13, brought to the fore traditional winter flavours and culinary delights to the people of Mysuru.
Conducted by Sahaja Samrudha and Sahaja Seeds at Nanjaraja Bahadur Choultry, the event has evoked a warm response from the public. The mela is showcasing winter crops such as groundnuts,avarekai,halasande,togari, roots and tubers,desimaize, and pigeon pea, apart from a variety of millets.
Different varieties ofavarekai—chinugalu, dabbe, kempu, mani,andhittala— relished by older generations but relatively unknown to the youth, were on display and for sale. The bulk of it has been cultivated in places around H.D. Kote, Periyapatna, Tumakuru, Dharwad, and Bengaluru Rural.
Dr. Shivaprasad Huded, Vice-Principal of JSS Ayurveda Medical College, inaugurated the Maghi Sambhrama and underlined the importance of consuming pulses and legumes during winter.
“It is essential to increase the intake of foods prepared from traditionally grown crops such asavarekai(field beans),halasande(cowpea), and pigeon pea pods. Their use benefits farmers who follow the multi-cropping system by enhancing their income, while consumers derive health benefits,” he added.
“The aroma and taste ofavarekaiand pigeon pea, available during the Maghi season, are truly special. These are protein-rich foods available at an affordable cost. Maghi Sambhrama has introduced traditional foods and cooking practices to urban residents. It should also be organised in other centres where the culinary culture associated withavarekaiis fast-disappearing,’’ said Dr. Huded.
Kalappa, an organic farmer from Hitnehebbagilu village of Periyapatna taluk, rued that cultivation of traditional crops such as groundnut, tree pigeon pea, and sweet potato, which require minimal care in cultivation, was becoming rare.
‘’Farmers, attracted to commercial crops like tobacco and hybrid maize, have forgottenavarekai,halasande, and tubers, and are becoming dependent on store-bought groceries. At least for their personal consumption, farmers should grow pulses and tubers,’’ he noted.
Maghi Sambhrama is not just an exhibition and sale of pulses and legumes. Visitors can also relish dishes such asavarekai uppittu, avarekai dosa, muddewith shelledavarekai sambar, avarekai bath,and evenavarekai jamun,in addition tojowar rottiof north Karnataka,’’ said Krishnaprasad of Sahaja Samrudha.
A salient feature of the Maghi Sambhrama is the availability of rare and indigenous varieties of rice, such asuduru sali, brought by the Devadhanya Farmers Producer Company. A display of bottle gourds in various shapes and sizes, apart from an exhibition of  ‘gourd art’ which entailed making artistic or decorative objects using gourd, are other attractions of the event, which will conclude on December 14.

title: Focus on coal price rationalisation, quality improvement and workers' welfare: Union Coal Minister G. Kishan Reddy tells SCCL
summary: Focus on coal price rationalisation, quality improvement and workers' welfare: Union Coal Minister G. Kishan Reddy tells SCCL
content:
Hyderabad
Union Minister of Coal and Mines G. Kishan Reddy called upon the Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) to immediately focus on reducing coal prices, improving coal quality, securing new mining blocks and strengthening workers’ welfare, to ensure the organisation’s long-term sustainability.
The Minister chaired a high-level review meeting on Singareni at Singareni Bhavan in Hyderabad on Saturday. Emphasising the need for timely reforms, Mr Kishan Reddy said that the Centre was in the process of introducing reforms in the coal sector and made it clear that public sector undertakings can survive only if they function with complete commitment and efficiency.
He said that new labour laws have been implemented with a focus on workers’ welfare and stressed the need for their strict and effective implementation. “There should be no compromise whatsoever when it comes to the welfare of Singareni workers,” the Minister asserted.
Since coal production remains the core business of Singareni, the Minister directed the company to enhance coal quality standards by setting up coal washeries, including the adoption of new dry washery technologies.
Earlier, Singareni Chairman and Managing Director Shri N. Balaram made a detailed PowerPoint presentation, explaining the company’s financial position and future strategies. The meeting was attended by Coal Ministry Secretary Vikram Dev Dutt, Telangana Energy Secretary Naveen Mittal, B. Veera Reddy, Director (Technical), ED (Coal Movement) B. Venkanna, among others.

title: Amaravati farmers’ issues will be addressed on priority, says Union Minister Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar
summary: Union Minister Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar prioritizes resolving Amaravati farmers' issues, with most land acquisition cases nearing resolution.
content:
Union Minister of State for Rural Development Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar has asserted that the government is committed to resolving the Amaravati farmers’ issues on priority basis through the three-member committee, with justice, transparency and farmers’ confidence as its guiding principles.
Addressing a review meeting at the APCRDA headquarters in Amaravati on Saturday, Mr. Chandra Sekhar said farmers’ problems were being classified into general and major issues, and examined in depth. He said nearly all of the 47 land acquisition cases under review had reached the resolution stage, and the remaining would be settled in a week.
As part of Amaravati’s capital requirements, acquisition of around 2,500 acres of land would be taken up in phases. He said that of the 69,421 land pooling plots, registrations for 61,793 plots had been completed, and issues related to the remaining would be resolved soon.
Mr. Chandra Sekhar said a proposal had been finalised for road alignment at Mandadam village after considering farmers’ views and suggestions from local MLA Tenali Sravan Kumar. He added that legal hurdles related to the lanka lands had been cleared to enable registrations, while a special committee was constituted to study soil and water levels in about 180 acres of Jareebu lands.
Municipal Administration and Urban Development Minister P. Narayana said social infrastructure development in Amaravati was a top priority, with DPRs for 26 villages under preparation. He said ₹22.6 crore had been sanctioned for 18 community halls, and assured clarity on road-hit lands, compensation and TDR bonds in three months.
Mr. Sravan Kumar said the government was in continuous dialogue with farmers and conducting regular reviews to address concerns related to land acquisition, village abadi lands and infrastructure development.

title: Revanth briefs Rahul on Telangana’s political situation
summary: Revanth briefs Rahul on Telangana’s political situation
content:
HYDERABAD
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy and Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) president B. Mahesh Kumar Goud received Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, at the Rajiv Gandhi International Airport (RGIA) and travelled with him to Hotel Falaknuma Palace on Saturday.
During the journey, Mr. Revanth Reddy and Mr. Goud briefed Mr. Gandhi on the latest political situation in the State. The duo informed him about the Congress party’s victory in the recent Jubilee Hills Assembly byelection and the strong performance of party-backed candidates in the first phase of the ongoing Gram Panchayat elections.
Mr. Gandhi has reportedly expressed satisfaction with the performance of the State government and the party. Mr. Gandhi was here to meet football legend Lionel Messi, who is visiting India as part of the GOAT India tour.

title: Family trio holds the key as voters deliver hung verdict in Pala municipality
summary: A family trio's unexpected victories in Pala municipality create a hung council, influencing the political landscape amid fierce competition.
content:
As the UDF and LDF locked horns in a high-stakes battle for control of the Pala municipality, a little-known family collective has stolen the spotlight, pulling off a stunning three-seat sweep.
The surprise winners are Binu Pulikkakkandam, a CPI(M) renegade, his daughter Diya Binu, and his brother Biju Pulikkakkandam. While Mr. Pulikkakkandam, a businessman-turned-politician, emerged victorious from Ward 14, Ms. Binu, an economics graduate from Madras Christian College who is preparing to pursue an MBA degree, has won from Ward 15.
His brother, who has worked closely with Union Minister Suresh Gopi for years, clinched Ward 13. The trio contested and won from three adjoining wards in the Thekkekkara region of the municipality, located across the Meenachil river.
With the UDF securing 10 seats and the LDF 11 in the 21-member council, the three Independent victories have assumed critical importance, as 14 seats are needed for a clear majority. “Both sides have approached us, but no decision has been taken yet. We will arrive at a decision after due consultations with our voters,” Mr. Pulikkakkandam said.
With a hung verdict and neither front in a position to form the ruling combine on its own, Ms. Binu has emerged as a strong contender for the chairperson’s post, with support from either the UDF or the LDF.
This is not the first time Mr. Pulikkakkandam has pulled off such a political coup. In 2010, he had led a mini independent collective in the same region, contesting alongside Independents Ranjini Pradeep and Latha Mohan, and made surprising inroads.
Over the past one-and-a-half decades, he has worn multiple political hats, serving as an Independent, a BJP councillor, and a CPI(M) councillor. A constant thread running through his political journey has been his fierce opposition to Jose K. Mani, chairman of the Kerala Congress (M).
Mr. Pulikkakkandam was expelled from the CPI(M) last year following months of friction over seat-sharing, after the KC(M), the dominant partner of the LDF in Pala, rejected the CPI(M)’s proposal to project him as municipal chairperson.
Adding to the narrative of young faces making an impact, attention has also turned to 24-year-old Riya Cheeramkuzhy, also known as Riyo Bino, who has won from Kaveekunnu on the Congress ticket.
An off-road driver with a deep passion for adventure sports, Ms. Bino inherited her love for jeep racing from her father, Bino Jose. Trained in driving from a young age, she obtained her driving licence at 18 and a heavy vehicle licence at 22, going on to make a name for herself in jeep racing circuits.
Interestingly, her father’s younger brother had earlier served as an LDF councillor in the Pala municipality.
